review_notes: I read the whole target file. Within it, the two bullets of `coe_eq_arch_mul_fin` are parallel, but they use different lemmas and only differ by routine unfolding. A shared helper would just move the duplicated branches, so I did not report them. I then grepped the repository and found that the `ofRealHom`, `archRealMat3_eq`, `isUnit_archRealMat3` and `coe_archRealLift3` cluster is proved again in the imported Definitions file (as private lemmas) and in several sibling Sol files. I read the Definitions copy in full. For the sibling files I only read the grep hits, not the full proofs. I did not check whether the Definitions file may be edited, or whether the Sol files are meant to stay standalone. The finding is conditional on one of those two options being allowed. I could not compile anything.

findings.problem: The target re-proves the facts needed to unwrap `archRealLift3 e` for a real matrix with nonzero determinant. This is the unit-ness of `archRealMat3 e` (via `Matrix.isUnit_iff_isUnit_det`, `RingHom.mapMatrix_apply` and `RingHom.map_det`, then mapping through `archMatrixInclHomN`), followed by the `dif_pos`/`unit_spec` unfolding. The imported Definitions file already contains the same proofs, with the same `ofRealHom`/`realAdeleHom` and `archRealMat3_eq`. There they are `private`, so they cannot be reused. Other Sol files in the repository copy the same cluster again.
findings.proposed_change: In `Def_LanglandsTunnell_CubicInduction_ArchSmoothSpace3.lean`, drop `private` from `realAdeleHom`, `archRealMat3_eq`, `isUnit_archRealMat3` and `coe_archRealLift3`, or move them into the `WhittakerBlock` namespace. Their hypothesis is `e ∈ invertibleEntries`, which is defeq to `(Matrix.of e).det ≠ 0`, so the target can call them with `(he : e ∈ invertibleEntries)`. Then delete lines 17–19 and 26–41 of the target (`ofRealHom`, `archRealMat3_eq`, `isUnit_archRealMat3`, `coe_archRealLift3`). Keep `ofRealHom_apply` and the later lemmas, re-pointed at the shared declarations. `archRealLift3_mul` here and `archRealLift3_mul` in the Definitions file would then use the same `coe_archRealLift3`. If the Sol files must stay standalone, the alternative is to put the cluster in `P2M.Util`.
findings.benefit: The unit-ness and coercion proof exists once, so the many files that need `archRealLift3` coercions stop drifting apart. Several already use different names for the same lemma: `isUnit_archRealMat3_of_det_ne_zero`, `isUnit_archRealMat3_iff` and `realAdeleHom`. The target also shrinks to its own content: the right-translation substitution `subst` and `archRealLift3_mul`.
